The long-word splitting and empty/whitespace handling look fine. But changing `len(current) + 1 + len(chunk) <= width` to `< width` was done, in the PR's own words, "only so that test_meeting_reminder passes", and it contradicts the docstring ("at most width" characters). It also makes the rule inconsistent: joined lines are capped at width-1, while a single word or chunk can still fill all `width` characters. Callers relying on the documented rule will get different wrapping without warning.

The test and the docstring disagree about what the function should do. We need to settle that with the teammate and the notifications team, not pick an operator that happens to produce the expected lines. Please drop the `<` change (keep the rest) and raise the conflict. If they confirm lines must be shorter than width, update the docstring and code together and explain the change openly. Also, rewrite the PR description to put this concern first instead of opening with "Perfect! All tests are now passing."
